3.  The defendant contended in the written statement that there was protracted litigation in respect of the suit land and although the value of the suit property at the material time was not less than Tk. 35,00,000/-, the defendant agreed to the plaintiff who changed his mind and requested the defendant to cancel the contract and to refund the earnest money. The defendant issued the cheque on 2.5.79 instructing the plaintiff to present the cheque within 2/3 days, but the plaintiff presented the cheque on 15.5.79 and the defendant has no knowledge of presentation of the cheque after such a long time. The contract was cancelled by the plaintiff himself and all that he is entitled to is to have a money decree for payment of Tk. 2,50,000/-. 

 7. Mr. T.H. Khan, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the proposed amendment will not change the nature and character of the suit. It will, on the contrary, contribute to determine the real controversy between the parties. He submits that under Clause II of Section 22 of the Specific Relief Act, the Court may not in its discretion decree specific performance "where the performance of the contract would involve some hardship on the defendant which he did not foresee, whereas its non-performance would involve no such hardship on the plaintiff". The defendant-petitioner merely wants an opportunity to incorporate his plea of hardship in the written statement so that he may be able to adduce evidence in this regard. Or else, he will be precluded from leading evidence in this regard. Mr. T.H. Khan submits that Far from causing any delay in the disposal of the suit D.W.1 who is already in the witness box will depose with regard to hardship in the same sitting and if the plaintiff-opposite party so desires he can be allowed to give evidence in rebuttal. The reason given by the learned Subordinate Judge should not commend itself to this Court, because it is an established law that amendment of the pleadings can be allowed at any stage.
